acts: Unicode Standard Annex #14, Unicode Line Breaking Algorithm, revision 57
Unicode Standard Annex #29, Unicode Text Segmentation, revision 49

en.title: UAX #14 rev. 57, Section 5.1 B2: is the Spanish parenthetical em dash a default behaviour or a tailoring?
en.summary: The B2 description says that in Spanish the dashes around a parenthetical should not be broken from the contained text; one paragraph earlier it says line breaks can occur before and after an EM DASH. The rules follow the first sentence: LB17 covers only B2 SP* × B2, and LineBreakTest.txt expects breaks between EM DASH and a following or preceding letter. The description does not say that the Spanish convention needs tailoring, and Section 8 does not mention it.
en.impact: “a —b— c”: the rules allow a line to end with the opening dash and to start with the closing dash.
en.correction: If the convention requires tailoring, say so in the B2 description and refer to Section 8.

quotes.text: Some languages, including Spanish, use EM DASH to set off a parenthetical, and the surrounding dashes should not be broken from the contained text.
Line breaks can occur before and after an EM DASH.

responsible.role: publishes the annex and the Unicode Character Database

ai_role.en: AI agents read the annexes and the data files and compared them; the examples were run through published implementations. An AI coordinator checked each place against the full annex and the trackers, and two further AI models checked the report before filing.
